model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents "#Iteration" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Five lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration. The purple line labeled "Vanilla" starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations, then gradually levels off, reaching approximately 2.50 by iteration 140,000. The blue line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)" follows a similar initial steep decline but plateaus at a notably higher loss, ending at approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000. The orange line labeled with a partially obscured legend (appearing to be another configuration) closely overlaps with the Vanilla line throughout most of the training, ending near 2.50–2.52. The green line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" also starts near 3.4 and follows a trajectory very close to the Vanilla line, ending at approximately 2.51 by iteration 140,000. The red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" similarly tracks close to the Vanilla line, ending at approximately 2.51–2.52. The dark blue line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" follows a path very similar to the Vanilla and other SepLLM variants, ending near 2.50–2.52. All lines exhibit shaded regions around them indicating variance or confidence intervals. The StrmLLM (n=64) line is distinctly separated above the cluster of other lines from roughly iteration 20,000 onward, while the Vanilla, SepLLM, and orange lines remain closely grouped together throughout training.
